hits.name: Tony Dinh
hits.hook: Price shock with a screenshot: 'Holy shit @cursor_ai is expensive'. 55 replies on 56 likes.
hits.draft_en:
Holy heck, extra SharePoint storage is expensive.

Microsoft charges about US$205 per TB a month once you go over your tenant's pool.

A lot of what fills it is files that haven't changed in two years.

That's why I built ArchiveBridge: it moves those files out for US$35 per TB and leaves a link that restores each one.
hits.video_tip: 20-30s screen recording: show Microsoft's own extra-storage price, then the ArchiveBridge price. Use a test tenant, no client names on screen.

hits.name: Tony Dinh
hits.hook: Speed brag: asked his bot to build an offline Hacker News iOS app and it finished before take-off. 102 replies.
hits.draft_en:
One question to ask your coding agent tonight:

"If the database was deleted right now, what exactly would we restore from?"

Not the code. Git has that.

The rows, the storage files, the auth users.

If the answer starts with "I think", you don't have a backup yet. Nearly 30 years in disaster recovery and that's still the question that catches people.
hits.video_tip: 30-45s face cam: read the question to camera, then show the prompt typed into your coding agent on a test project. Captions on for sound-off scrollers.

narrative_synthesis: Stories and stances beat news today. levelsio's Uber-driver story pulled over a million views on plain first-person dialogue, then he rode it with a follow-up. Greg's 'saas is becoming free, charge for the agent that does the work' got saved like a manifesto. Tony's Cursor price shock and before-take-off app build show cost and speed still pull replies. Nobody on the list is talking about what happens when the agent breaks something, which is Nick's lane.
